issues.problem: The fix for the control-file stamp issue is a short, case-sensitive denylist. A repo-controlled query_state_file/usage_state_file can still name other SB control files in the state dir, and case variants pass. (1) orchestrator-directive.json: a graphify query overwrites the blocking orchestrator directive with an epoch; sb_orchestrator_directive_is_blocking (jq '.blocking == true') is then false, so orchestrator-directive-guard.sh no longer blocks, without the audited SB OVERRIDE. (2) 'Trivial' / 'TRIVIAL': on macOS's default case-insensitive APFS this is the legacy trivial marker, so the original exploit (stop-check, ci-status-check, planning-file-guard and subagent-stop disabled) still works with a one-letter change. (3) planning-edit-override, roadmap-edit-override, mode, skill-invocations, outcomes-session.json, edit-without-workflow.count, e2e/release live-matrix files are also accepted. docs/CONSENT.md claims stamps are 'never for one of SB's control files'.
issues.evidence: bash REVF-H4a-r2-probe/scripts/stamp.sh (graphify enforce consent; record-graphify-query.sh on 'graphify query x'): orchestrator-directive.json -> contents '1793728622', 'NOT-blocking' (it was {"next_skill":"silver-plan","blocking":true}); planning-edit-override, roadmap-edit-override, mode, skill-invocations, outcomes-session.json, Trivial, TRIVIAL, STATE are each created under that name; only sub/../trivial, ./trivial, trivial/ and x/../state fall back to graphify-query. The case-insensitive macOS effect is static reasoning (this host is case-sensitive).
issues.suggested_fix: Stop honouring arbitrary names. Either ignore query_state_file/usage_state_file and always use the built-in <tool>-usage / graphify-query names, or accept only a basename matching ^[a-z0-9-]+-(usage|query)$ compared after lowercasing (or inside a dedicated $SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR/opt-in/ subdirectory). Tests that use custom stamp names can switch to names that match the pattern. Add tests for orchestrator-directive.json, planning-edit-override and a case variant, and correct the docs/CONSENT.md row.

issues.problem: (a) Stale-lock takeover is racy. Two waiters that both see a dead owner can both 'rm -rf' the lock; the second removes the lock the first has just taken, both enter the critical section, and an update is lost. (b) A lock dir without a pid file, left by a process killed between mkdir and the pid write, is never taken over, so every later write fails after 10 s until the user removes it. The message does say how. (c) A non-numeric SB_CONSENT_LOCK_TRIES aborts with 'unbound variable', exit 1.
issues.evidence: bash REVF-H4a-r2-probe/scripts/lock2.sh (lock dir containing a dead pid, then 7 parallel 'grant <tool> --all-projects --capabilities enforce'): rounds granted=6, 7, 4, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7 (lost updates in 2 of 8). lock.sh: a pid-less lock with SB_CONSENT_LOCK_TRIES=5 -> rc 2; SB_CONSENT_LOCK_TRIES=abc -> 'line 172: abc: unbound variable', rc 1.
issues.suggested_fix: Take over a stale lock atomically: mv the stale lock to a unique name, then rm it, and retry mkdir. Only the waiter whose mv succeeds proceeds; recheck the pid after the mv. Treat a pid-less lock older than N seconds as stale. Validate SB_CONSENT_LOCK_TRIES as an integer.

issues.problem: Delivery and install detection are still regexes on the raw string. Commits slip past through git global options other than -c/-C, aliases, ANSI-C quoting, backslash-escaped subcommands and commit-creating porcelain. Machine-wide installs slip past through other pipe targets and package managers. The quote stripping and the leading-'$' rule also cause small false positives. All of this is limited to the opt-in gates; completion-audit still gates commits.
issues.evidence: bash REVF-H4a-r2-probe/scripts/fp.sh REVF-H4a-r2-probe/scripts/byp-cmds.txt (all 5 gates, enforce consent, tools not ready). Allowed: git --no-pager commit, git --git-dir=.git commit, git -c alias.ci=commit ci, git com\mit, git $'commit', git commit-tree/merge/am/cherry-pick/revert; npm -g install, npm install --location=global, brew reinstall, pipx/cargo/go/gem install, pip install --user; curl ... | /bin/bash, | env bash, | python3, bash <(curl ...), sh -c "$(curl ...)". Also allowed: writes the heuristic analyzer misses (dd of=, F=x; echo > $F, truncate, rsync, patch, git apply, git checkout --). Denied (false positives): '$PYTHON -m pytest', '"$PY" -m pytest tests', 'cd src && $EDITOR a.py'.
issues.suggested_fix: After F2 merges, take delivery, install and write classification from F2's tokenizing analyzer (actions and opaque flags) or from completion-audit's command classifier, not from regexes. At least allow any git global option before the subcommand, and treat a pipe into any shell or interpreter path as an install. Do not treat a variable program word that is only an interpreter path as delivery.
